about: A first-person narrator, a woman, named only by the other characters addressing her ('Thessaly'); the name is no glossary character when the brief is suggested, so the code cannot yet verify her gender from it, and it can once the Names step lists her.
title: The Hill Farm Winter
author: Corin Ashdown

chapters.title: The First Snow
paragraphs: I woke before the others, as I always did on the hill farm, and lay listening to the wind in the chimney.
Dov was already in the yard. I could hear him breaking the ice on the trough with the heel of his boot.
"Hold the rope tight, Thessaly," he called up to the loft, and I took the end of it in both hands.
I pulled until my shoulders ached. The sack of feed swung up through the hatch and I dragged it across the boards.
Brin came in from the barn stamping the snow off his boots. He nodded to me and said nothing, which was his way.
"Thessaly says she will take the east pasture today," Dov told him, and Brin grunted his agreement.
I tied my scarf and pulled on the old coat that hung by the door. It smelled of smoke and sheep.
The east pasture lay under a clean white sheet, and I walked out across it counting the ewes.
"Careful on the slope, Thessaly," Brin shouted from the gate, and I raised one hand without turning round.
By noon I had found all but one. I went back along my own tracks and found her in the lee of the wall.
I carried her home across my shoulders. She was light, and she bleated twice, and then she was quiet.
"Where is Thessaly?" Dov asked when I did not come to the table. "She went out for the ewes, and she said she would be an hour."
I came in then, with snow on my hair and the ewe still warm against my neck, and the kitchen went quiet.
Dov looked at me for a long moment. Then he laughed, and pulled out the chair beside his own.
